WHAT I CONCLUDED, ON WHAT EVIDENCE:
1. Mechanism of the cosmetic `failed command:` line — PROVEN at source + repro. A `.zig_test` run's child stderr is piped and captured; `evalZigTest` sets `run.step.result_stderr` on the SUCCESS path (Run.zig:1719), and `build_runner.zig:1381-1388` calls `printErrorMessages` for any step with non-empty result_stderr, which prints the step as `w` and then `failed command: <argv>` (build_runner.zig:1516-1520). Exit status stays 0. Minimal repro at /tmp/weizigo/t351-experiment: a passing test calling `std.debug.print("HELLO-STDERR…")` yields `run test w` + the line + `failed command:` + EXIT 0. So the noise is cosmetic and the suite is already green where these tests run.
2. stdout is NOT an escape hatch — PROVEN. stdout is the Zig 0.16 test-runner IPC protocol channel (`waitZigTest` reads `std.zig.Server.Message.Header` structs from child stdout). Repro: a passing test that writes to stdout via `Io.File.Writer` and FLUSHES hung the runner (the flushed text is read as a header with a bogus ~1.4GB bytes_len and the runner blocks in the 60s response-timeout wait); the same write WITHOUT flush silently discards (buffered, never flushed) and emits nothing. So diagnostics can reach the run log only via stderr, which is exactly what produces the warning.
3. Bars 1 and 5 are mutually exclusive — CONCLUDED. Bar 1 (zero `failed command:` lines) requires no stderr from test binaries; bar 5 (keep `[EXPECTED]`/`I4/I5/I7/I9` evidence in the suite output) requires the evidence to be emitted somewhere the run log can see it; the only such channel is stderr. Hence eliminating the noise == deleting the evidence. This is precisely the case the refresh anticipated ('if the only way … is to suppress them, stop and report').
4. The noise is still present at HEAD — ESTABLISHED. HEAD's five files still carry ungated `std.debug.print` (colex.zig:192; rules.zig:562,959,963,964,981,985,986,1027,1040,1050; vb_graph.zig:497-499,585,595,660,937,970,972,1086,1104 plus the main demo block 1131-1168; vb_mutants.zig:117,155,183,210,239,249,282,295,330,345; vb_fixpoint.zig:497,512,521,532,542). The mechanism is deterministic, so the ~8 cosmetic lines will reproduce at HEAD.
